verdict.rationale: Angular's docs say the framework is 'organized yet modular thanks to Angular components and dependency injection'. Community posts back this up: they describe encapsulated, reusable components, modular code via @Input/@Output, and built-in dependency injection that eases testing. Some community criticism targets the older AngularJS module and injector design (global namespacing, an under-documented provider system), which lowers confidence but does not concretely contradict current Angular. Missing for 10: in-depth first-party DI and provider documentation in the pack (only a marketing tagline), and recent hands-on corroboration of modern Angular's DI and modular architecture.
